# PlanWorldSimulator world generator

Describe a planning benchmark in plain language and generate a playable world from it.
See [docs/design-decisions](docs/design-decisions) for the architecture.

The generator is a fake for now: it walks through the real steps (storyline, copy
template, fill template, tests) and writes a world folder, but does no LLM work.

## Layout

| Path                  | What it is                                                  |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `src/web`             | Website (Vite, React, TypeScript, Tailwind)                 |
| `src/backend`         | API (FastAPI, SQLite via SQLAlchemy and Alembic)            |
| `src/worlds-template` | Base template every world is copied from                    |
| `src/worlds`          | Generated worlds, one folder each (contents are gitignored) |

## Run it

```sh
just up      # build, start in the background, wait until healthy
just down    # stop (database and generated worlds are kept)
```

Open http://localhost:8480 (API docs on http://localhost:8400/docs). If another program uses
those ports, `just up` says so; set `PLANWORLDSIMULATOR_WEB_PORT` and
`PLANWORLDSIMULATOR_API_PORT` in `.env` to change them. Other commands: `just build`, `just logs [service]`,
`just ps`, `just reset` (also deletes the database volume) and `just dev` (live
reload, site on http://localhost:5173). Copy `.env.example` to `.env` to change
defaults.

## Develop

Needs [pixi](https://pixi.sh), [pnpm](https://pnpm.io) and [just](https://just.systems).

just install
just format
just lint
just typecheck

# Leaderboard plan

This plan fits what's already in the repo. Each world runs its own server behind `/play/{id}/`. Each world's `Game` already exposes `score()`. The backend keeps an anonymous creator cookie, stored as a hash in `creator_hash`.

## Core idea

Each world has its own leaderboard, because scores aren't comparable across different worlds. Each difficulty level (1–3) gets its own board too. Seed is the one thing that shouldn't split boards. Seeded worlds are reproducible, so boards can be per `(world, level, seed)` for fair comparison, with an "all seeds" average view as an option.

## 1. Data model (new migration `0005_runs.py`)

**`players`**
- `id`
- `display_name`
- `token_hash`: the anonymous cookie, same pattern as `creator_hash`
- `created_at`

**`runs`**
- `id`
- `world_id` (FK)
- `level`
- `seed`
- `player_id` (FK)
- `kind`: `human` or `agent`
- `agent_name` (nullable)
- `score`
- `weeks`
- `metrics` (JSON: served %, cash, and so on)
- `status`: `in_progress`, `finished` or `abandoned`
- `started_at`
- `finished_at`

Add an index on `(world_id, level, seed, score DESC)`.

## 2. Anti-cheat: the server decides the score

The browser must never submit its own score.

- When a human or agent starts a run, the world's `Game` creates a `run_id`.
- When the episode ends, the world server calls the backend directly: `POST /internal/runs/{run_id}/finish`. It sends the score and metrics, authenticated by a per-world shared secret from env, on localhost only.
- The backend validates that the run exists and is `in_progress`, and that the seed and level match. It then stores the result.
- Because both the UI and MCP call the same `Game` methods (decision 0004), human and agent runs go through one path. The `kind` field says which was which.
- Because runs are seeded, an optional later step is to replay the logged actions in a fresh env to verify a score.

## 3. API (new `api/leaderboard.py`)

- `GET /worlds/{id}/leaderboard?level=&seed=&kind=&limit=` returns ranked rows with rank, name, score, weeks and kind.
- `GET /worlds/{id}/leaderboard/me` returns the caller's best runs and rank.
- `POST /players/me` sets or changes the display name. It creates the player cookie on first use.
- Ranking: highest score wins. Ties go to fewer weeks, then to the earlier finish. Best run per player is the default view, with an "all runs" toggle.

## 4. Identity

- **v1:** an anonymous cookie plus a chosen display name, with no login. This matches the current creator-cookie approach.
- Names get a length limit, trimmed whitespace and a small profanity filter.
- **Later:** optional OAuth to claim a name and carry it across devices.

## 5. Frontend (`src/web`)

- A **Leaderboard tab** on the world page. It has level and seed selectors and a human/agent/all filter. It highlights "you" and shows your rank when you're outside the top N.
- An **end-of-run screen** with the score, your rank, "Play again" and "Same seed again". Add a name prompt on a first finish.
- A **"Beat the agent" badge**: agent runs are shown alongside humans, which supports the "Agent vs You" idea.
- **Home page:** the featured worlds can show their current top score.

## 6. Hardening

- Rate-limit the finish and name endpoints.
- Abandon `in_progress` runs after a timeout so they don't pile up.
- Only the world server's secret can finish a run. Reject the second finish of a run.
- Moderation: an admin-only delete for a run or a name.
- Cache boards for a few seconds. At this scale SQLite is fine.

## 7. Delivery order

1. Write a short design decision record, `0006-add-per-world-leaderboards.md`, using `docs/design-decisions/template.md`.
2. Add the migration, models and the internal finish endpoint, with tests.
3. Add the public leaderboard and player endpoints, with tests.
4. Add the world template's `Game` hook that starts a run and reports it when it ends. The template is in `src/worlds-template`, so every new world gets it.
5. Build the web leaderboard tab and end-of-run screen.
6. Hardening, then agent runs with `agent_name`.

## Questions

- **Boards:** do you want boards per `(world, level, seed)`, or per `(world, level)` with a fixed daily or weekly seed for everyone, like a daily challenge? The daily seed gives the strongest "everyone played the same game" feel.
- **Agent runs:** should they share the same board as humans, or be separate?

# Leaderboard plan (v2: one board per world and level)

**Changes from v1:**
- Boards are keyed by `(world, level)`.
- Seed no longer splits boards.
- The seed selector is gone.

## Fairness decision

Seed changes demand, lead times and hidden-rule parameters (decision 0004). If everyone plays a random seed, a lucky seed decides the ranking. I recommend this rule:

- **Ranked runs use one fixed seed per `(world, level)`.** The backend chooses it, and it is stored on the world as `ranked_seed_L1..L3`, or derived from `world.seed` and the level.
- **Free play with any seed is still allowed.** It is recorded but doesn't appear on the board.

This gives everyone the same game on a board, with no extra aggregation logic. If you'd rather let people pick any seed and rank on a combined number, tell me. That would need a normalised score and more machinery, so I'm not planning it.

## 1. Data model (migration `0005_runs.py`)

**`players`**
- `id`
- `display_name`
- `token_hash`: the anonymous cookie, same pattern as `creator_hash`
- `created_at`

**`runs`**
- `id`
- `world_id` (FK)
- `level` (1–3)
- `seed`
- `ranked`: true when the seed equals the ranked seed
- `player_id` (FK)
- `kind`: `human` or `agent`
- `agent_name` (nullable)
- `score`
- `weeks`
- `metrics` (JSON)
- `status`: `in_progress`, `finished` or `abandoned`
- `started_at`
- `finished_at`

Add an index on `(world_id, level, ranked, score DESC)`.

## 2. Anti-cheat

The browser never submits a score.
- The world's `Game` creates the `run_id` at start. It reports the final score to the backend with `POST /internal/runs/{run_id}/finish`, using a per-world secret from env, on localhost only.
- The backend checks that the run is `in_progress` and that the level and seed match. A second finish is rejected.
- Human (REST) and agent (MCP) runs go through the same `Game` path.
- Later option: replay the logged actions in a fresh env to verify a score.

## 3. API (`api/leaderboard.py`)

- `GET /worlds/{id}/leaderboard?level=1..3&kind=&limit=` returns rank, name, score, weeks and kind. It only includes `ranked` runs.
- `GET /worlds/{id}/leaderboard/me?level=` returns your best run and rank for that level.
- `POST /players/me` sets the display name and creates the cookie on first use.
- Ranking: highest score wins. Ties go to fewer weeks, then to the earlier finish. The default shows each player's best run. An "all runs" toggle is optional.

## 4. Identity

v1 uses an anonymous cookie plus a display name. Names get a length limit, trimmed whitespace and a basic profanity filter. OAuth to claim a name across devices can come later.

## 5. Frontend (`src/web`)

- The world page gets a **Leaderboard tab** with a Level 1/2/3 switch and a human/agent/all filter. It highlights you and shows your rank if you're outside the top N.
- Starting a level from the world page launches the ranked seed by default. A "Free play" option picks a custom seed.
- The **end-of-run screen** shows the score, your rank, "Play again" and the name prompt on a first finish. It says clearly when a run was unranked.
- Agent runs appear on the same board with an agent badge. The kind filter can hide them. This is the default unless you say otherwise.
- Featured worlds on the home page show the current top score for each level.

## 6. Hardening

- Rate-limit the finish and name endpoints.
- Abandon stale `in_progress` runs after a timeout.
- Admin-only delete for a run or a name.
- Cache boards for a few seconds. SQLite is enough at this scale.

## 7. Delivery order

1. Write `docs/design-decisions/0006-add-per-world-level-leaderboards.md` from `template.md`, covering the ranked-seed rule.
2. Add the migration, models, ranked-seed assignment and the internal finish endpoint, with tests.
3. Add the public leaderboard and player endpoints, with tests.
4. Add the `Game` hook in `src/worlds-template` that starts and finishes runs, so every new world gets it.
5. Build the web leaderboard tab and end-of-run screen.
6. Hardening, then agent runs with `agent_name`.

## Open questions

- Are you happy with fixed ranked seeds per `(world, level)`? It's the main thing that changed from v1.
- Should agent runs share the human board (my default), or have a separate one?

I can start on step 1 and step 2 if you'd like.
